But several statements are unsupported or contradict the card, and an investigator would need to re-check them.","problems":["Claims the elevated 99215 share 'appears in every complexity stratum' - true, but the packet's by_complexity rows show 0-condition share of 19.5% vs 2.1% overall, which is fine; however the 'a legitimately complex panel would not look like this' is a strong assertion.","C0017371 is described as a 0-condition UTI visit documented as high MDM; the card lists C0017371 as 99215 supported with 47 minutes and high MDM, and the low-complexity list shows it as N39.0 with 0 conditions, so that part holds, but it is not among the cited claim IDs and is not listed in the examples.","Recommends pulling documented 99215s on 0-1 condition patients (C0017371, C0017168, C0017256), yet C0017371 is not in cited_claim_ids, so the citation does not tie to the examples listed.","Cited examples C0017168 and C0017256 are described as 'patient aged 49/48 with 0 chronic conditions', consistent with the card; C0017337 has no age or condition details, and the card does not show it in the low- or high-complexity lists, so its relevance to low-complexity billing is unsupported.","Only 3 of the 6 cited claims have documentation; the other 3 (C0017076, C0017107, C0017110) support only low complexity, not anything about documentation, and C0017213, C0017235, C0017190 named in the text are not cited.","Says 'The rule check found many notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab' but the figure is 15 of 41 (37%), and 'many' is loose; this is a weak rule-based flag and the text repeats it twice.","Next step 'sampling plan in the recovery packet' refers to an item not in the evidence; the narrative also says 'targeted records request for undocumented low-complexity 99215' without naming which claims; the text is repetitive and a bit contradictory ('does not settle it' then 'fits upcoding')."]}
